claim: In Cheiro's system the heart line relates to the affectionate disposition and the emotional side of love.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The Line of Heart relates purely to the affectionate disposition, in fact, to the mental side of the love nature of the subject.

claim: A heart line reaching the Mount of Jupiter is read as idealistic, loyal and principled in affection.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: People with such a Heart Line are firm and reliable in their affections, they have an unusually high code of honour and morality.

claim: A heart line ending between the first and second fingers is read as a calm but deep, self-sacrificing affection.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: gives a calmer but a very deep nature in all matters of the affections

claim: A heart line ending on the Mount of Saturn is read as reserved, undemonstrative and self-focused in love.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: They are inclined to be cynical, reserved, undemonstrative but very insistent in trying to gain the person they want.

claim: An extremely long heart line is read as a tendency toward jealousy and intense attachment.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: When the Line of Heart is found in excess, namely, extremely long--it denotes a terrible tendency toward jealousy

claim: A shorter heart line is read as less outward expression of the higher sentiments of affection.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The shorter the Line of Heart is on the Hand, the less the higher sentiments of the affection make themselves manifest.

claim: A deep, clear heart line is the form Cheiro considers healthy for the affections.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The Line of Heart should be deep, clear, and well coloured.

claim: A thin or pale heart line is read as coolness or reserve in affection.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: When the Line of Heart is very thin and with no branches, it denotes coldness and want of heart.

claim: When the heart line lies low, close to the head line, feelings tend to interfere with reasoning.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: When very low down on the hand, almost touching the Line of Head, the heart will always interfere with the affairs of the head.

claim: A heart line that forks between Jupiter and the space below the first two fingers is read as a balanced, happy affectionate disposition.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: it is an excellent sign of a well-balanced, happy, affectionate disposition

claim: A broken heart line is traditionally read as a period of deep emotional upheaval in relationships.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480

claim: Cheiro treats the head line as the most important line, indicating mentality and the direction of thought.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The Line of Head ... or indication of the Mentality of the subject, must in all cases be considered as the most important line on the hand.

claim: A head line joined to the life line at its start is read as a sensitive, cautious nature that tends to undervalue its own talents.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: a highly sensitive disposition, which inclines towards the side of caution and also lacks self-confidence

claim: A head line starting slightly apart from the life line is read as independence of thought, quick judgement and mental daring.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: it is an excellent mark to have, giving independence of thought, quickness of judgment, and a certain mental daring

claim: With the head line separated from the life line, Cheiro stresses that such people need a clear purpose to channel their quickness.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: these people with the "open Line of Head" must, above all things, have purpose in their life.

claim: A straight head line is read as practicality, conventional thinking and determination to carry plans through.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The straighter the Head Line is found, the subject can be more relied on to carry out his determination

claim: A head line sloping toward the Mount of the Moon is read as an imaginative, artistic and romantic temperament.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: This form is largely found on the hands of artists, painters, and those who even in other walks of life have the sensitive artistic temperament

claim: A clean, deep head line is read as strong mental concentration; fine clear lines are associated with brain workers.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: A clean cut deep Line of Head is a more powerful sign of mentality than when the line is very broad

claim: A broad or shallow head line is read as less concentration and a more changeable nature.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: A wide broad line shows less concentration and a more vacillating changeable nature.

claim: A forked head line is read as a balance between practical and imaginative thinking, sometimes with indecision.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: this forked mark often indicates a certain want of decision.

claim: A long, well-marked head line is read as greater mental aptitude and range.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: With a Line of Head long and well marked, it increases all the promise of mental aptitude and success

claim: In Cheiro's system the life line relates to vitality and constitution rather than a fixed lifespan.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: to be normal the Line of Life should be long, clearly marked, and without any irregularities or breaks of any kind.

claim: A long, clearly marked life line is read as vitality and strength of constitution.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: Such a formation would indicate length of life, vitality, freedom from illness, and strength of constitution

claim: A life line sweeping in a wide curve into the palm is read as robust energy and warmth.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: whether it forms a well-defined curve or semicircle out into the palm

claim: A life line hugging the thumb and narrowing the Mount of Venus is read as a more delicate constitution.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: In the first case it indicates a naturally more delicate constitution, and less force of animal magnetism.

claim: A clear, thin, deep life line is read as nerve and will-force, more resilient than a broad shallow line.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: such an indication is not nearly as good a sign as a clear, thin, deep line.

claim: A broad, shallow life line is read as physical strength with less staying power under strain.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The broad Life Line seems to belong to people who have more robust animal strength

claim: A life line rising high toward the Mount of Jupiter is read as self-control and an ambitious nature.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: the subject has more control over himself, and his life is more governed by the ambitious side of his nature.

claim: Breaks in the life line are traditionally read as periods of change or reduced vitality; Cheiro reads them alongside other lines.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480

claim: A fate line rising from the wrist straight toward Saturn is read as a strong sense of direction; Cheiro considers it most fortunate with a good Sun line.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: luck, brilliance, and success will attend the Destiny, and extreme good fortune may be anticipated.

claim: A fate line rising from the Mount of the Moon is read as an eventful, changeable career influenced by other people.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: the Fate will be more eventful, changeable, and largely depending on the fancy and caprice of other people.

claim: A fate line starting in the middle of the palm is read as success won through one's own hard work.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: such a person will be the architect of his own fortunes

claim: A break in the fate line where the new piece overlaps the old is read as a change of position that can bring advancement.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: it foretells a complete change in surroundings and position

claim: When no clear fate line is visible, Cheiro reads the destiny as less marked by outside events.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480

claim: A clear Sun (Apollo) line is read as magnetism, recognition and success.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: People with the Sun Line appear to have more magnetism, more influence over others.

claim: A Sun line rising from the fate line is read as recognition earned through personal effort.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: it is a sure sign of recognition for the career adopted, but brought about by the personal effort of the subject.

claim: A well-developed Mount of Jupiter is read as a desire to lead, organise and achieve distinct goals.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: When large, it shows desire to dominate, to rule and command others, to lead and organise

claim: With a weak head line, a large Mount of Jupiter is read as pride and self-opinion.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: a large Mount of Jupiter gives pride, excess of vanity

claim: A developed Mount of Saturn is read as prudence, quiet determination and love of solitude and serious study.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: Its chief characteristics are love of solitude, prudence, quiet determination, the study of serious sombre things

claim: A flat Mount of Saturn is read as a lighter, less serious outlook on life.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: A complete absence of this Mount indicates a more or less frivolous way of looking at life

claim: A well-developed Mount of the Sun (Apollo) is read as a desire to shine, enthusiasm for beauty and a sunny, generous temperament.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: When large or well developed it indicates glory, publicity, a desire to shine before one's fellows.

claim: A developed Mount of Mercury is read as quickness of mind, wit, eloquence and aptitude for science and commerce.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: It gives quickness of brain, wit, thought, eloquence. It also relates to adaptability in science and commerce

claim: A developed Mount of the Moon is read as imagination, romance, idealism and a love of travel and change.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: This Mount relates to everything that has to do with the imaginative faculties, the emotional artistic temperament, romance

claim: A well-formed Mount of Venus is read as a desire for love and companionship, warmth and love of beauty.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: When well-formed and not too large, it denotes a desire for love and companionship, the desire to please, worship of beauty

claim: A flat Mount of Venus is read as a cooler, less passionate temperament.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: This Mount is therefore called Positive when high or large, and Negative when small or flat.

claim: A developed lower (first) Mount of Mars is read as a martial, competitive nature with leadership drive.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: These subjects are born fighters in every sense of the word.

claim: A strong lower Mount of Mars is also read as a hasty temper that passes quickly.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The temper is hasty and explosive, but at the same time quickly over

claim: A developed upper (second) Mount of Mars is read as moral courage and quiet determination; better organisers than leaders.
source_name: Cheiro, Palmistry for All (1916), Project Gutenberg #20480
source_wording: The latter type are mentally very courageous, and possess _moral courage_ more than physical.

claim: An index finger longer than the ring finger is commonly read in palmistry as a Jupiter emphasis: ambition and a wish to lead.
source_name: General palmistry convention, paraphrased

claim: A ring finger longer than the index finger is commonly read as an Apollo emphasis: creativity and willingness to take risks.
source_name: General palmistry convention, paraphrased

claim: A long thumb is traditionally read as strong will power and the capacity to direct one's own life.
source_name: General palmistry convention, paraphrased

claim: A square palm with short fingers (earth hand) is read as practical, reliable and hands-on.
source_name: Modern elemental hand classification (20th-century palmistry convention), paraphrased

claim: A square palm with long fingers (air hand) is read as communicative, analytical and curious.
source_name: Modern elemental hand classification (20th-century palmistry convention), paraphrased

claim: A long palm with short fingers (fire hand) is read as energetic, enthusiastic and action-oriented.
source_name: Modern elemental hand classification (20th-century palmistry convention), paraphrased

claim: A long palm with long fingers (water hand) is read as sensitive, intuitive and imaginative.
source_name: Modern elemental hand classification (20th-century palmistry convention), paraphrased
